prompt: What is the primary benefit of pipelining many commands in one request?
explanation: A pipeline packs many commands into one round trip: instead of paying one network round-trip time per command, the client pays roughly one per batch. It saves I/O latency, not server CPU, and it does not make the batch atomic.

options.text: Many commands share one network round trip instead of paying one round trip each
Pipelined commands execute atomically as a group
The server caches pipelined responses to speed up repeats
Pipelining moves command execution to a worker thread pool
